title: Classifying matter
caption: A pure substance has a fixed composition: an element (one kind of atom) or a compound (elements chemically joined in fixed proportions). A mixture can be separated by physical means and may be uniform throughout (homogeneous) or not (heterogeneous).
alt: A tree: is the sample one substance? Yes leads to: can it be broken down chemically? Yes, compound; no, element. No leads to: is it uniform throughout? Yes, homogeneous mixture; no, heterogeneous mixture.
description: Is it a single pure substance with fixed composition?
If yes: can chemical reactions break it into simpler substances? Yes, a compound such as water or sodium chloride; no, an element such as oxygen or iron.
If no, it is a mixture: uniform throughout is homogeneous, such as salt water or air; otherwise heterogeneous, such as sand in water.
